Formulation  
Patient presents with recent onset viral-type illness (sore throat, runny nose, dry cough, night sweats, mild fever initially) causing fatigue and some anxiety about symptoms. Stress related to work is present but described as positive and not contributing to mood disturbance. No psychiatric symptoms identified. Physical illness has temporarily affected function and motivation. Supportive factors include good insight, stable social and occupational functioning, and no significant psychiatric history.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  
Principal Problem: Mild fatigue and stress associated with acute viral illness and increased work demands  
- Patient Goal(s): Recover physical health and maintain stable mood and work performance  
- Clinical Goal(s): Symptom resolution of viral illness; support stress management as needed  
- Actions (Patient): Rest; take a few days off from work; maintain hydration; use Paracetamol/Ibuprofen as needed; monitor symptoms; return for follow-up if symptoms worsen or persist beyond one week  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide reassurance and advice regarding self-care; monitor for symptom progression; advise on when to seek urgent care (e.g., worsening breathlessness, chest pain, high fever); offer mental health support if stress or mood symptoms emerge
